slug: 2020-01-01 ID4D Diagnostic of ID Systems in Tunisia (World Bank)

facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic states that civil registration is conducted by local governments and centralised in the Madania database run by the Ministry of Local Affairs and the Environment (MALE), with the National Informatics Center (CNI) responsible for its technical implementation; the report says its contents are current as of September 2019.

The World Bank diagnostic states that MALE, the technology ministry (MTCEN) and CNI have developed a strategy to upgrade Madania, including a move to a paperless system and linked birth, marriage and death records, with the new system to be developed over 2020 and deployed during 2021; contents current as of September 2019.

The World Bank diagnostic states that data on births, deaths and marriages are entered into Madania by local officials, and cites MALE (2019) for 18.53 million birth acts, 4.14 million death acts and 3.8 million marriage acts recorded as of 2018.

The World Bank diagnostic states that civil events are recorded at municipal level in physical ledgers and then manually entered into Madania by local officials, in a hierarchical local, regional and central database synchronised in nightly batches; contents current as of September 2019.

The World Bank diagnostic states that as of 2015 Madania, first deployed in the municipality of Tunis in 1992 and rolled out nationally from 2004, was accessible from nearly 481 sites (all municipalities plus regional and commercial sites) and 1,300 workstations, used by about 1,500 people; it gives 264 municipalities before 2016 and does not say how many offices register in it.

The World Bank diagnostic lists among 2019 milestones the launch of the procurement process for the redesign of the civil registration system (Madania), with implementation planned for 2020 and full-scale implementation for 2021.

systems.platform: SQL Server; three separate databases for births, deaths and marriages/divorces
systems.owner: Ministry of Local Affairs and the Environment (MALE); technical implementation by the National Informatics Center (CNI)
systems.tiers: municipal civil registration offices, then regional, then central; nearly 481 sites and 1,300 workstations as of 2015; 350 municipalities since the 2016-2018 reform, delegations having registered in rural areas until 2018
exchange of birth extracts between government agencies: piloted with the Ministry of Education, used by CNRPS and CNSS since March 2019

systems.system: Madania data transfers to other bodies
systems.platform: text file, FTP server or physical media
systems.tiers: to the electoral authority (ISIE), to the National Institute of Statistics for vital statistics, and to the CIN database on request

systems.system: Online request for birth certificate copies
systems.owner: MALE with MTCEN, CNI and the Tunisian Post
systems.tiers: national online request using the CIN number, paper copy sent by post or collected in person; partially operational since 2018

systems.platform: biographic database developed in-house in Cobol; turnkey biometric image database
systems.tiers: applications at local police stations and national guard offices; data entry and card printing at 31 regional offices; central office
planned; draft law withdrawn in early 2018, no date announced as of late 2019

systems.country_label: Registre de l'Identifiant Unique du Citoyen (RIUC); identifiant unique citoyen (IUC)
systems.owner: MALE as project owner with MTCEN; implemented by CNI; later a management body (OGI) under MALE
systems.tiers: central register of nearly 15 million records built from Madania and the CIN database; first version in production September 2019, queried by social-sector and education systems

systems.platform: national interoperability platform modelled on Estonia's X-Road
